newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Night watchman files suit against Swiss banker.
newsitem.headline: Night watchman files suit against Swiss banker.

text.p: A night watchman who snatched old documents bound for the shredder at a Swiss bank in the belief he was aiding the search for Holocaust accounts has filed a suit against the bank's chairman, his lawyer said on Friday.

The suit alleges Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) chairman Robert Studer maligned bank guard Christoph Meili by questioning the watchman's motives for spiriting the papers out of Switzerland's biggest bank, lawyer Marcel Bosonnet said.
The suit, which was mailed on Friday, was filed "for violating Christoph's individual rights", Bosonnet said. He did not specify what damages the suit sought.
A bank spokeswoman said the suit was unfounded. "This is absolutely untenable," she said.
The suit stems from Studer's remark on Swiss television last week that Meili may not have acted solely for noble motives.
"What I now know makes me suspect that the reasons Meili has given for his actions are not the only ones," Studer said. He did not elaborate when asked what he meant.

UBS says the destruction this month of old records from a subsidiary it acquired in 1945 was a "regrettable accident" and insists no client records were lost that could assist the search for any dormant wealth of Holocaust victims in Swiss banks.

Meili smuggled bank documents out of UBS headquarters and gave them to Zurich Jewish leaders, who alerted prosecutors. They are now investigating whether UBS broke a ban on destroying relevant records or if Meili violated Swiss banking secrecy.
